svg.text: Ex4DGS: the change surface for K = 1 → K intervals
What has to change, what does not, and the four places that would silently undo it.
CUDA layer — NO CHANGE
The extension receives one already-evaluated scalar opacity per primitive and has no time concept at all. K is invisible to it.
rasterize_points.cu:41 · only cull is the per-pixel alpha < 1/255 at forward.cu:380 · sorts on the ORIGINAL primitive index
This is the single biggest reason to build here rather than on Multi4D, where the temporal gate is inside the kernel.
Python layer — where the work is
(a) parameterisation
_opacity_duration_center [N,2,1]
_opacity_duration_var [N,2,1]
→ [N,K,2,1], and bump
self.opacity_degree = 2
every literal [:,0] / [:,1] must follow
(b) the alpha(t) evaluation
utils/interpolations.py:55-61
SEVEN LINES. That is the whole gate.
· max / noisy-OR over per-interval plateaus
· do NOT inherit .min(dim=1) — already
wrong on the left tail at K=1
(c) keyframe layout
NO CHANGE NEEDED
trajectories are indexed by absolute time,
not by interval — a primitive re-enters at
whatever pose it has interpolated to
_xyz_motion [N,37,3]
(c) is also the hazard
nothing optimises the trajectory
across a gap — no gradient
reaches it there — yet
expand_duration and motion_reg
extrapolate smoothly THROUGH it
Four places that would silently undo a multi-interval presence — in priority order
1. densify_and_split:945 / densify_and_clone:1007 reset var to the constant 2 and jitter center. A naive repeat at K>1 duplicates all intervals identically
→ multi-interval structure destroyed every 300 iterations. This is the one most likely to eat the mechanism without any error.

2. adjust_temp_opa:1338 uses .any(dim=1) — one edge-abutting interval doubles the variance of all of them. 3. extract_..._from_static:1180 hardcodes a 2-element stack, so new primitives are born K=1. 4. load_ply:633 allocates from opacity_degree; extra intervals are discarded.
Why K=1 is structural, not a tuning limit
The plateau is selected by a sign test:
where((c0 - t) · (c1 - t) < 0, 1.0, tail)
That product is negative on exactly one interval for any
(c0, c1), and the tails are monotone away from it.
Two disjoint presence intervals are not representable
at any parameter value. This is the claim the thesis rests on.
Effort summary
CUDA kernels to edit ................. 0
core gate function .................... 1 file, ~7 lines
parameter shape + index sites ......... ~6 call sites
structural ops to make K-aware ........ 4 (the bypasses above)
Contrast Multi4D: the gate is in CUDA, hard-culls at 0.05 in
forward AND backward, so an absent primitive gets no gradient.
Source: research-wiki/operations/ex4dgs-code-map-2026-09-19.md §2, §6 · verified against the checkout at commit 7fac649
Caveat worth keeping in view: none of this speaks to whether K>1 helps. It says only what the edit costs and where it would silently fail.
